# Primary-source lock — Nakamura's completed Riemann zeta distribution

Source: Takashi Nakamura, *A complete Riemann zeta distribution and the Riemann hypothesis*, Bernoulli **21** (2015), 604–617; arXiv:1504.03438; DOI 10.3150/13-BEJ581.

Imported status: **PUBLISHED PRIMARY-SOURCE THEOREM**  
Created: 2026-08-12  
RH status: **unproved**

## 1. Completed xi characteristic function

Nakamura defines

\[
 \Xi_\sigma(t)=\frac{\xi(\sigma-it)}{\xi(\sigma)}.
\]

His Theorem 1.1 proves that `Xi_sigma` is a characteristic function for every
real `sigma`, with an explicit positive density obtained from the classical
Riemann theta integral.

The completed Fisher source used in `L-91309` is exactly this law:

\[
 E(z)=\xi\!\left(\frac12+z\right),
 \qquad
 \varphi_a(t)=\frac{E(a-it)}{E(a)}
 =\Xi_{1/2+a}(t).
\tag{N-2015.1}
\]

Thus the repository probability source is Nakamura's completed Riemann zeta
distribution at

\[
 \sigma=\frac12+a.
\]

## 2. Explicit safe-range quasi-Levy representation

For every `sigma>1`, Nakamura's Theorem 1.4 gives

\[
 \boxed{
 \Xi_\sigma(t)
 =\exp\left[
  it\lambda_\sigma+
  \int_0^\infty
  \left(e^{itx}-1-itx\mathbf1_{x\le1/2}\right)
  d\nu_\sigma(x)
 \right],
 }
\tag{N-2015.2}
\]

with explicit drift `lambda_sigma` and signed quasi-Levy measure

\[
 \boxed{
 d\nu_\sigma(x)
 =q_\sigma(x)\,dx+dN_\sigma(x),
 }
\tag{N-2015.3}
\]

where

\[
 \boxed{
 q_\sigma(x)
 =\frac{e^{-\sigma x}}x
  \left[
   \frac1{1-e^{-2x}}-(1+e^x)
  \right]
 }
\tag{N-2015.4}
\]

and

\[
 \boxed{
 dN_\sigma(x)
 =\sum_p\sum_{r\ge1}
  \frac{p^{-r\sigma}}r\,
  \delta_{r\log p}(dx).
 }
\tag{N-2015.5}
\]

The atomic part is precisely the positive compound-Poisson Levy measure of the
ordinary Euler ratio `zeta(sigma-it)/zeta(sigma)`.

## 3. Exact one-sign-change archimedean channel

Put `y=e^x>1`. The bracket in (N-2015.4) is

\[
 \frac1{1-e^{-2x}}-(1+e^x)
 =\frac{1+y-y^3}{y^2-1}.
\tag{N-2015.6}
\]

Let `varpi` be the plastic constant, the unique real root greater than one of

\[
 \varpi^3-\varpi-1=0,
\]

and put

\[
 \kappa=\log\varpi=0.281199\ldots.
\]

Since `y^3-y-1` is strictly increasing for `y>1`,

\[
 \boxed{
 q_\sigma(x)>0\quad(0<x<\kappa),
 \qquad
 q_\sigma(x)<0\quad(x>\kappa).
 }
\tag{N-2015.7}
\]

The sign boundary is independent of `sigma`.

Consequently the Jordan decomposition is explicit:

\[
 \boxed{
 d\nu_\sigma^+
 =dN_\sigma+q_\sigma(x)\mathbf1_{0<x<\kappa}dx,
 }
\tag{N-2015.8}
\]

\[
 \boxed{
 d\nu_\sigma^-
 =-q_\sigma(x)\mathbf1_{x>\kappa}dx,
 \qquad
 \nu_\sigma=\nu_\sigma^+-\nu_\sigma^-.
 }
\tag{N-2015.9}
\]

Both are positive Levy measures. Near zero `q_sigma(x)=O(x^{-2})`, while at
infinity its negative part is `O(e^{-(sigma-1)x}/x)`, so

\[
 \int_0^\infty (1\wedge x^2)d\nu_\sigma^\pm(x)<\infty.
\]

## 4. Safe-range divisibility theorem

Nakamura proves that for every

\[
 \sigma>1,
\]

the characteristic function `Xi_sigma` is

```text
quasi-infinitely divisible,
but not infinitely divisible.
```

Therefore for every Suzuki-safe scale `a>1/2`, the repository law
`varphi_a=Xi_(1/2+a)` is a positive probability law and a quasi-ID law, but it
is not generated by one nonnegative Levy measure.

By uniqueness of the Levy--Khintchine triplet, no alternative single positive
Levy measure represents the same completed law.

## 5. Prime score is a direct summand of the positive channel

At a prime-power atom

\[
 x=r\log p=\log(p^r),
\]

one has

\[
 x\frac{p^{-r\sigma}}r
 =\Lambda(p^r)(p^r)^{-\sigma}.
\]

For `sigma=1/2+a`,

\[
 \boxed{
 a x\,dN_\sigma(x)
 =d\beta_a(x),
 }
\tag{N-2015.10}
\]

where `beta_a` is the exact ordinary-prime scattering-score measure of
`L-91307`.

Thus the ordinary-prime Poisson first chaos is not merely analogous to the
completed quasi-Levy source. It is an orthogonal direct summand of the positive
part `L2(nu_sigma^+)`, after radial scoring by `a x`.

## 6. Repository consequence

The theorem blocks the shortcut

```text
completed Fisher law = one positive prime Poisson law.
```

But the explicit Jordan decomposition gives a stronger constructive
replacement:

```text
positive channel:
  ordinary-prime atoms + short archimedean jumps;
negative channel:
  long archimedean jumps;
deterministic channel:
  explicit drift lambda_sigma.
```

All three are explicit and zero-free in the safe half-plane. The signed
completion can therefore be represented at tangent level by a positive direct
sum of two Levy first-chaos spaces plus one scalar drift channel, with the sign
stored in the observation rather than in the metric.

## 7. Source boundary

Imported directly from Nakamura:

```text
Xi_sigma is a characteristic function for every real sigma;
formula (N-2015.2)--(N-2015.5);
Xi_sigma is quasi-ID but not ID for sigma>1;
the ordinary zeta ratio has positive atomic Levy measure N_sigma.
```

Local deductions:

```text
varphi_a=Xi_(1/2+a);
q_sigma changes sign once at log(plastic constant);
nu_sigma has the explicit positive Jordan split (N-2015.8)--(N-2015.9);
a x N_sigma=beta_a, so the prime score is a direct positive summand.
```
